articles.body: PRESS REVIEW – Friday, September 25: There's anticipation and excitement in France as Pope Leo XIV embarks on the first papal visit to France in 18 years. It comes at a time of renewed Catholic faith among young French people. Also, we look at reactions after Italy's new legislation banning full-face Islamic headwear from schools. Plus: US rapper Macklemore announces a new "Free Palestine" tour that will raise funds for humanitarian groups.
articles.headline: US rapper Macklemore announces 'Free Palestine' tour after Ed Sheeran saga

articles.body: Alison Sargent is pleased to welcome Andrea Antonio Verardi, Professor of Church History and Cultural Heritage at the Pontifical Gregorian University. According to Verardi, Pope Leo’s visit to France is much more than a diplomatic visit. The focus of the visit combines three key issues: the search for peace amid geopolitical instability, the challenge that artificial intelligence and technological change pose to humanity and human dignity, and the unexpected re-emergence of religious identification among younger generations in a deeply secular society.
articles.headline: Pope Leo visits France: Pontiff wants to focus world's attention on peace, human dignity, technology

articles.body: Paris is making final preparations for Pope Leo XIV's first official visit to the French capital in 18 years, with volunteers welcoming crowds ahead of his four-day trip. articles.body: Pope Leo XIV's visit to France is forcing Emmanuel Macron into a delicate diplomatic balancing act. There will be no private meeting between the two leaders — officially because of the Pope's packed schedule — and Macron is not expected to attend any of the religious services during the visit. articles.body: President Donald Trump is tentatively set to visit Alabama for a political rally next week, a curious move in a deep-red state as his party fights for control of Congress in several battlegrounds. The event is penciled in for Oct. 2 in Mobile, but the plans have not yet been finalized and are subject to change, according to two people with direct knowledge of the preparations who were granted anonymity to disclose private planning. An October rally in Alabama would be a somewhat confounding decision for the president. The GOP has found itself having to play defense in their own territory recently, with Democratic candidates are seriously competing for Senate seats in normally red states like Alaska and Texas. But Alabama has not been considered a state where Democrats have any real shot at winning any statewide office. Spokespeople for the White House and Republican National Committee did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The rally could help shore up support for state Rep. Rhett Marques, who is locked in a somewhat competitive race with Democratic Rep. Shomari Figures. Marques is still seen to have the advantage after the Supreme Court allowed the state to use a House map that reconfigured Figures’ majority-Black district earlier this year. Mobile, though, is outside of that district. Marques’ campaign and Figures’ campaign did not respond to requests for comment. A foray into Alabama would not be the first time that the president has tried to shore up support in a solidly Republican state this cycle — he rallied last month in South Carolina for Sen. Darline Graham during her primary runoff — but as the general election season has begun he has also started to visit battleground states. Last week, he rallied alongside GOP Senate nominee Michael Whatley in North Carolina. Trump’s potential campaign visit would follow Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy’s announcement last week that the Trump administration has granted a $2.5 billion loan to the Alabama Toll Road, Bridge, and Tunnel Authority. That money will fund the construction of the Mobile River Bridge — the largest infrastructure project in the state’s history. The president is also fond of GOP Rep. Barry Moore, who is running for Senate in the state. Another close ally, Sen. Tommy Tuberville, is the Republican nominee for governor. He’s running against Democratic former Sen. Doug Jones, who he unseated in 2020.
articles.headline: Trump eyes an October campaign rally — in Alabama

articles.body: Republicans’ 2024 gains among young men have evaporated — and that could have instant ramifications this November, according to a new Cygnal poll . President Donald Trump narrowly carried young men in 2024, according to exit polls , a big swing toward the GOP from past elections. But Democrats’ generic ballot lead among men ages 18-30 who say they are the most determined to vote now sits at 57%-40%, according to the poll. Trump’s favorability is underwater at just 38%-55%, and Republicans’ net favorability among the demographic now sits at -9 points, with 40% viewing the party favorably and 49% unfavorably. One silver lining for the GOP: Among all registered voters sampled, including those least likely to turn out in November, the Democratic generic ballot lead is much smaller, 44% to 41%. “It is not a very good electorate, if you're the Republican Party, among the people who are the most determined to vote,” said Alex Tarascio, pollster and principal at Cygnal, in an interview with POLITICO ahead of the poll’s release during Thursday’s Symposium on Young American Men. Young men alone likely won’t determine control of Congress; they make up a fraction of the electorate, and they are less likely to vote than women of the same age or their older counterparts. But that lack of enthusiasm itself is a warning sign for Republicans, who will need to motivate their base ahead of November if they wish to maintain control of Congress. The young men sampled are overwhelmingly concerned about cost-of-living issues — the same reason that many swung toward the GOP two years ago. When given a list of options and asked which will matter most in determining their vote in November, a wide plurality — 29% — selected “inflation and the cost of living,” and another 14% chose “housing costs and being able to afford a place to live.” When asked what policies would make the biggest difference in their lives, the top answers again deal with the economy: The most-selected options were lowering the cost of goods, lowering housing costs and cutting taxes. Many young men feel pessimistic about their ability to achieve success. When asked if they feel the rules in this country are set up to work for or against young men, 43% said they feel the rules are set up against them to 47% who said the rules are set up in their favor. That pessimism bleeds into how they view other institutions. Both the Democratic Party (-1) and Republican Party (-9) have net-negative favorability among the demographic, and the White House’s current occupants are even more unpopular: Vice President JD Vance sits at 37% favorability with -10 net favorability, while Trump is at 38% favorability with -17 net. “Young men are pretty down on institutions and political figures, and this one isn't any exception to that,” Tarascio said. Republicans successfully targeted young men and low-propensity voters in 2024 to help propel them to victory largely in part by having Trump sit for interviews with podcast hosts and influencers popular with young men. Trump has yet to return to those forums en masse ahead of the midterms, but he’s repeatedly told voters to pretend as if he’s on the ballot in November. But Trump may no longer be the motivator he once was for turning out young, male, low-propensity voters. Among those surveyed who were least likely to vote, Trump’s net favorability is -22, lower than the respondents most likely to vote, where his net favorability is -19. “If Trump gets in front of them, I don't think it's a bad bet, but for some of these people it could backfire,” Tarascio said. The poll was conducted Sept. 15-18 with a sample of 800 registered male voters ages 18-30. The margin of error is plus or minus 3.46 percentage points. CORRECTION: A previous version of this article misstated that this poll had a likely voter screen. Democrats have a 57%-40% lead among men ages 18-30 who say they're the most determined to vote.
articles.headline: Young men are swinging away hard from Republicans, pessimistic about economy, new poll finds

articles.body: Q THE LANDSLIDE: Quinnipiac University released a poll today that found Gov. Kathy Hochul leading Republican Bruce Blakeman 58-39 — putting her on track for the fourth-largest landslide by a New York gubernatorial candidate in the past 200 years. It’s by far the best poll for Hochul this year and certainly better than a Siena University survey out this morning that found her with a modest 9 point lead over the Nassau County executive. So which one’s closer to reality? The last time both pollsters released New York numbers on the same day was a few weeks before Hochul’s last election in 2022. Siena found at the time that her lead over then-Rep. Lee Zeldin was quickly shrinking, having dropped from 17 to 11 points. The Q Poll painted a more dire picture for the governor. “We released a poll in mid-October showing that Hochul had a 4 point lead over Lee Zeldin,” Quinnipiac spokesperson Mary Snow said. “And it went against the grain of other polls out there at the time.” Hochul wound up winning that race by about 6 points. Pollster vs. pollster results in prior elections have been mixed. Both Q and Siena nailed Andrew Cuomo’s eventual 23 point margin of victory in October 2018 polls, though Siena’s early November numbers that year found Cuomo’s lead had shrunk to 13. An infamous Q Poll from September 2010 found Cuomo with a stunningly small 6 point lead over Buffalo firebrand Carl Paladino, while a Siena poll the next day found a much more predictive 57-24 Cuomo advantage. The biggest difference this time around is that Quinnipiac assumed a higher share of November’s turnout will be in deep blue New York City. The five boroughs accounted for 31 percent of the statewide turnout in 2022 and 34 percent in 2018. Siena’s sample assumed 30 percent of this year’s voters will come from there, while 38 percent of Quinnipiac’s sample was from the city. Quinnipiac also does more to avoid undecided voters. “One tweak that we made after 2020 was an adjustment to the questions that we ask, so that we try to cut down on the number of people who say they don’t know,” Snow said. Only 3 percent of the Q Poll’s sample declined to weigh in on the Hochul-Blakeman race, while the comparable number was 9 percent in Siena’s poll. And it appears as if a lot of the Quinnipiac respondents who might not have answered Siena’s questions broke toward the incumbent: Siena has Hochul winning New York City 61-27 while Quinnipiac has her up 70-27; Siena had her up 57-34 among women while Quinnipiac found her lead at 63-34. Another notable difference between the methodologies that may account for the divergent results is that Quinnipiac’s sample was based on asking respondents what party they affiliate with. Siena uses voter registration files. “For a couple of years running, the New York Times/Siena Poll was ranked as the most accurate poll in America,” Siena spokesperson Steve Greenberg said. “Siena has been polling New York state for nearly a quarter of a century, and we have shown that we get it right almost all of the time.” Republicans, for their part, believe both sets of numbers are far overstating Hochul’s advantage. “Blakeman is closer in the polls I’ve seen than Lee Zeldin was at this moment in time four years ago,” state Senate Republican Campaign Committee Chair George Borrello said. “As I travel around New York state, I have seen literally thousands of Bruce Blakeman signs. Yet I can count on one hand the number of Kathy Hochul signs I’ve seen, unless you count the ones that say ‘Fire Hochul.’” — Bill Mahoney From the Capitol MEGAWATT DEAL: New York has made its first awards for large-scale batteries under a new program and secured contracts for new renewables that are close to getting built. The state’s energy authority contracted for 719 megawatts from 13 solar, wind and hydroelectric projects and 950 megawatts of battery storage from eight projects. NYSERDA President and CEO Doreen Harris announced the awards Wednesday during a Climate Week event hosted by the state’s renewable developers association. “Everything that we do with respect to our energy system costs money,” Harris said. “When we invest in clean energy, not only are we talking about low single-digit percentage increases in cost, we are talking about benefits that far exceed those costs.” Hochul warned that federal headwinds and rising expenses made a more ambitious pace of transitioning to clean energy too costly as she successfully fought to weaken New York’s ambitious climate law earlier this year. But she has highlighted her continued support for progress on offshore wind, renewables, storage and nuclear this week. New York and developers are racing the expiration of federal tax credits. Renewables that didn’t start construction by July 4 — or don’t finish work by the end of the year if they start after that deadline — won’t be eligible for those key incentives that lower the cost of contracts for the state. Read more from POLITICO Pro’s Marie J. French here. FROM CITY HALL MAKING ROOM: Bellevue Hospital announced a major renovation and expansion of its inpatient psychiatric wing, fueled by an infusion of $25.6 million from the City Council. Bellevue, which is part of the NYC Health + Hospitals system, will use the new capital funding to add 40 beds for adult psychiatric patients over the next few years — bringing the division’s total capacity to 204 beds. Hospital officials said the expansion will ease the bottleneck of patients with severe mental illnesses who need to be admitted for continued observation and treatment; those inpatient psychiatric units have been operating consistently at 98% capacity. “The need here demanded an investment of this scale,” Council member Virginia Maloney, who spearheaded the funding, said during a news conference in the hospital’s atrium. Bellevue Hospital CEO Eric Wei said the facility has seen a bump in psychiatric patients since the April 2025 closure of Mount Sinai Beth Israel several blocks away. Bellevue’s dedicated ER for psychiatric patients, which Wei said sees about 30 patients daily, is undergoing its own $40 million expansion. “We are unfortunately needing to transfer out about 90 patients a month to other inpatient units because there’s no room in our inpatient psychiatric units,” Wei said in an interview. “We’re always feeling like I’m toeing the line. We’re very busy.” Bellevue was so overwhelmed as of late that hospital officials asked FDNY to stop bringing them patients with psychiatric emergencies, according to EMS union Local 2507. articles.body: A small group of White House officials is exploring whether to cut back President Donald Trump’s decision to increase foreign beef imports, as GOP panic rises ahead of the midterms. The proposal to reduce the amount of imports is being discussed within the Domestic Policy Council headed by Vince Haley, a longtime Trump speechwriter and former campaign official, and a few other officials at the White House, according to two people with direct knowledge of the conversations, who were granted anonymity to share private details. Trump officials are unsure if anything will come of the talks. The two people said the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative disagrees with cutting back the imports, since it aims to lower high consumer beef prices in the short term and since USTR helped implement the move. But their conversations about partly rolling back the beef policy — which Trump instituted in August — is a clear sign the White House is trying to stem the alarm from battleground and farm-state Republicans as high prices and Trump’s tariffs roil their election campaigns. The White House is also preparing a plan on diesel exports, likely with exemptions, amid sky-high prices from the Iran war. The White House and USTR, in statements after this article published, denied that there was any official action on the table. “There’s no pending policy change to ‘disagree’ with," a USTR official said. “The administration is focused on the interest of American ranchers and consumers. All agencies are supporting the President in these goals." “The White House is not considering such action. As the President directed in his executive order, the USDA and USTR continue to monitor beef imports to ensure that savings are being passed onto consumers,” White House spokesperson Kush Desai said. Earlier this week, Iowa Rep. Ashley Hinson, the GOP Senate nominee, took the extraordinary step of publicly breaking with Trump, saying gas prices were too high because of the Iran war and that farmers in her state are suffering. Michigan Senate GOP nominee Mike Rogers and other vulnerable House and Senate Republicans have made similar breaks. Farm-state lawmakers in Iowa and beyond have publicly called for the White House to provide some relief from the beef import executive action in particular, because of its impact on farmers and ranchers. Sen. Chuck Grassley, the rest of the Iowa delegation and other senior farm-state lawmakers have all pressed the administration to change course — to no avail. Trump did sign an executive order of rancher-friendly policies as a way to address the initial backlash. But U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer made clear to a group of House Republicans in a closed-door briefing earlier this month that Trump’s executive action to import 300,000 metric tons of beef without certain tariffs and at discounted prices would go forward as planned, as POLITICO first reported.

articles.body: The cryptocurrency industry is at a political crossroads. Reeling from the demise of its longtime top legislative priority, crypto companies must now decide how scorched-earth to go against Senate Democrats, who last week voted unanimously against the so-called Clarity Act, a sweeping bill that would create a bespoke new regulatory framework for digital assets. A crypto-backed PAC network’s move this week provides a hint of what may be to come. The group, known as Fairshake, announced it would spend at least $30 million to help block Democrat Sherrod Brown from recapturing a pivotal Ohio Senate seat, representing the first major signal of how the industry plans to deploy its massive campaign war chest in the final weeks before the 2026 midterms. Some crypto executives have publicly signaled an appetite in recent days for punishing Democrats. But a partisan strategy carries major political risk for the industry: A broad offensive against Democrats ahead of an election where they have a chance to reclaim power on Capitol Hill could further alienate lawmakers the industry may soon need to revive its agenda. “As much as some people may want to, they can’t wave a wand and make Democrats go away,” said Sheila Warren, the former CEO of the Crypto Council for Innovation, an industry trade group. “Every industry — not just crypto — has to figure out what to do with that reality.” The crypto industry’s spending could have immediate consequences after the election. Democrats are signaling that a Senate GOP-aligned spending spree would suppress any appetite for lame duck dealmaking involving the Clarity bill — although it remains a long shot that it would come back to life regardless. A Senate Democratic aide involved in the crypto effort said a full-scale assault on the party’s Senate candidates “would absolutely eviscerate any hope” of a post-election deal. The Fairshake PAC group, funded primarily by crypto firms Coinbase and Ripple and venture capital giant Andreessen Horowitz, had more than $120 million at its disposal as of the end of August. It has previously deployed its war chest to help members of both parties who support industry-friendly policies. Fairshake is preparing to announce additional spending decisions supporting both Democrats and Republicans in the coming days, according to a spokesperson for the group, Geoff Vetter. But it’s unclear what races — or which chamber — it will target next. Kara Calvert, Coinbase’s vice president of U.S. policy, said in an interview that bipartisanship has been crypto’s “superpower.” “Nobody is eager to erode that,” she said. Though Fairshake says it will maintain a bipartisan approach, it hasn’t specified what shape that will take. One potential avenue for the PAC is to continue to back crypto-friendly Democrats running for the House — where the Clarity bill advanced with 78 Democratic votes last year — but primarily help Republicans in the Senate. Fairshake spent in favor of several Senate Democrats in the 2024 elections, including in battleground general election races in Michigan and Arizona, where it backed Democratic Sens. Elissa Slotkin and Ruben Gallego, respectively. It also plowed more than $40 million into the effort to help defeat Brown in his 2024 reelection campaign — by far its biggest spend of the cycle. This time, Republicans are pressing the industry to recalibrate its approach and ditch the Democrats. “To reward people who voted against the motion to proceed on Clarity after the Democrats got 126 amendments in the bill would be a huge mistake,” said Sen. Cynthia Lummis, the crypto bill’s leading champion in the Senate. The Wyoming Republican is retiring when her term ends in January. Democrats, who feel increasingly confident about their chances in November despite the GOP’s spending advantages, say Republicans are trying to play the crypto industry. It’s “been the goal of Republican colleagues all along to try to get folks to invest in races, versus them trying to get a piece of legislation done, and someone needs to call the Republicans out on their bullshit,” said Sen. Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), who added: “Sherrod’s gonna win.”

articles.body: Les operadores privades de bicicletes d’ús compartit es resisteixen a desaparèixer de Barcelona, malgrat l’ anunci de l’Ajuntament d’eliminar aquest servei a partir del 2027 , però el consistori es manté ferm en la decisió. Fonts municipals assenyalen que aquest estiu s’han batut rècords de sancions imposades a aquests vehicles. Al mes de juliol se’n van posar 922 i a l’agost 702. La grua municipal va retirar, en aquests dos mesos, mig miler de bicicletes mal estacionades. En total, des del gener del 2025 s’han tramitat més de 7.000 sancions. També et pot interessar Barcelona imposa prop de 5.500 multes en poc més d’un any a empreses de lloguer compartit de bici Jordi Escofet 2 minuts de lectura Una patrulla conjunta Les empreses, però, asseguren que aquest estiu han intensificat la presència de la patrulla conjunta que van crear a finals del 2025 entre les set empreses que treballen a Barcelona . Remarquen que aquesta iniciativa és pionera a Europa i que “complementa els equips i mecanismes de control que cada operador aplica individualment, amb l’objectiu de prevenir i corregir incidències d’estacionament”. Un equip de betevé ha fet un seguiment d’aquesta patrulla conjunta per veure com treballen al carrer. També et pot interessar Junts, BComú, ERC i PP demanen a Collboni que no elimini les bicicletes de lloguer compartit a BCN Roger Torres i Liñán 1 minut de lectura Una bicicleta al fons del mar La primera bicicleta que retira la patrulla conjunta és una que el Servei Marítim ha tret del fons del mar, al costat de l’espigó del Gas, entre la platja del Somorrostro i la de la Barceloneta. De fet, no és la primera vegada que es localitza un vehicle d’aquest tipus sota el mar, també ha passat altres vegades amb el servei públic del Bicing . La patrulla conjunta recull la bicicleta i, en aquest cas, la carrega a la furgoneta per portar-la al taller. Bicicleta d’ús compartit trobada al fons del mar, al costat de l’espigó del Gas. Foto: Jordi Escofet En altres casos, la patrulla conjunta de les operadores es desplaça als aparcaments en forma d’U invertida per aparcar correctament les bicicletes . Quan aquests estacionaments estan plens mouen als vehicles a altres aparcaments propers que estan més buits. Si detecten alguna incidència a la bicicleta, com una roda punxada, també la carreguen a la furgoneta per portar-la a reparar. També et pot interessar El govern Collboni desoeix l’oposició i eliminarà el “bikesharing” de Barcelona el 2027 Roger Torres i Liñán 2 minuts de lectura Les operadores demanen que l’Ajuntament rectifiqui Roger Montañola, portaveu de les operadores privades de bicicletes d’ús compartit de Barcelona , remarca que han engegat la iniciativa de la patrulla conjunta per “voluntat pròpia”. D’aquesta manera, volen que “el funcionament del servei sigui millor i que les externalitats negatives que s’han pogut produir històricament, bàsicament en forma d’aparcament per part d’alguns usuaris, es corregeixin”. Montañola insisteix que volen seguir a Barcelona i que “no té cap sentit” que una ciutat “que es diu sostenible i moderna elimini un terç del seu parc mòbil de bicicletes , tenint en compte que l’altre és el Bicing, que per molt que vulgui créixer no està en disposició de fer-ho aviat”. Des del consistori, asseguren que en el proper contracte del Bicing —l’actual acaba el 2028—, la flota s’incrementarà un 50 % per arribar a les 12.000 bicis. També han fet arribar al consistori la proposta de fer aparcaments amb marques a terra específics per les bicicletes d’ús compartit, sobretot a les zones més cèntriques de la ciutat on hi ha més concentració d’aquests vehicles.

articles.body: Les darreres informacions en què s’explica que el Sant Andreu no va deixar entrar samarretes del Reial Madrid dimecres passat a l’ empat contra el Madrid Castella han generat rebombori a les xarxes. Alguns mitjans van acusar el club quadribarrat de no deixar entrar amb samarreta els seus aficionats a Can Dragó i l’ explicació és senzilla: el conjunt blanc no va demanar cap entrada visitant per al partit . El Reial Madrid no va demanar cap entrada visitant per al partit contra el Sant Andreu El Sant Andreu fa tres anys que prohibeix dur símbols de l’equip rival fora de la grada visitant . És a dir, a la zona habilitada per a l’afició rival, els aficionats poden mostrar samarretes, bufandes o banderes del seu equip amb total normalitat, però no ho poden fer a la resta de l’estadi. Es recorda que està prohibit accedir a Can Dragó amb qualsevol samarreta d'equip de futbol que no sigui del Sant Andreu. — Unió Esportiva Sant Andreu (@uesantandreu) September 23, 2026 Dimecres, al Sant Andreu – Reial Madrid Castella, el 100 % de l’aforament el formaven socis del Sant Andreu, ja què no es va vendre cap entrada al públic general . El club quadribarrat va anunciar a xarxes la mesura que fa anys que aplica i alguns aficionats es van queixar sense conèixer la realitat. Fet que determinats mitjans van fer servir per generar notícia i avivar la polèmica. També et pot interessar Moment màgic a Can Dragó: l’afició del Sant Andreu il·lumina l’estadi durant una apagada inesperada Marina Garrido 1 minut de lectura La realitat és que, com expliquem, el Sant Andreu fa anys que manté aquesta política. Des del club asseguren que desitgen veure simbologia visitant al seu estadi, però no a la grada local i encara menys d’equips grans com el Reial Madrid o el Barça, perquè no comparteixen amb ells la gran majoria de valors . El Sant Andreu explica que ja va viure una situació similar la temporada passada contra el Barça Atlètic, en què el club blaugrana va posar a 23 euros les entrades visitants per als aficionats quadribarrats, alhora que destaca que d’altres filials sí que ha col·laborat i s’han arribat a acords pels preus de les entrades, com pot ser el del Vila-real.

El correfoc de la Mercè es farà: dissabte 26 de setembre, a les 20.30 h, al passeig de Gràcia. Començarà amb la  Ceptrotada , l’encesa conjunta dels ceptrots, forques i estendards més espectaculars de cada colla, que portaran en Llucifer, la Diablessa, el Diable Gros i la resta de personatges singulars dels grups participants. Es tracta del mateix recorregut que va haver-hi en l’edició de l’any passat. A banda, hi haurà el correfoc infantil , per als més petits (el mateix dissabte, a les 18 h). Dimensions històriques! El correfoc de la Mercè estrenarà la porta de l’infern més gran de la seva història Manel Carrasco 2 minuts de lectura Recomanacions per al correfoc Si vols ballar sota la pluja d’espurnes del Correfoc, tingues present un seguit de recomanacions : Vesteix amb màniga llarga i pantalons llargs : com més coberta la pell, millor, sempre amb roba de cotó (el material sintètic es pot inflamar). Porta un mocador de cotó per tapar el coll, un barret per protegir el cap i també calçat adequat, com sabatilles esportives o de muntanya. Protegeix bé els ulls i les orelles  dels trons: unes ulleres i uns taps poden ser molt útils. Ni alcohol ni vidre : si tens set, porta líquids sense alcohol i evita els recipients de vidre, ja que si es trenquen poden representar un perill. Els infants, a distància : els infants s’ho passaran millor en el correfoc infantil, però si també aneu al correfoc, que estiguin sempre lluny de la primera fila i del foc. No llancis aigua  a les persones assistents al correfoc. Si tens una emergència : si pateixes una cremada o no et trobes bé, a la zona sempre hi haurà serveis mèdics i ambulàncies preparats per atendre. Una tradició que es remunta al 1979 El correfoc de la Mercè va néixer el 1979 com a Mostra de Bèsties Fantàstiques, dins el projecte de renovació i popularització de la Festa Major de la ciutat, i ràpidament es va convertir en un fenomen multitudinari i simbòlic de la Mercè. Per exemple, es faran sessions de showcooking amb Rafa Peña , xef i propietari de Gresca i Premi Nacional de Gastronomia, també amb Wenbin Peng , cuina de Shanghai amb mirada mediterrània, i Artur Martínez , Estrella Michelin, del restaurant Trü . L’escenari Mercè acollirà cinc concerts que recorren estils i geografies diverses amb el directe festiu d’ Azucarillo Kings , el flamenc contemporani del ballarí i coreògraf Marco de Ana , Sorvina que fusiona rap, jazz, neosoul i gòspel, la timba i el son cubà de Tumbakin i el jazz d’autora de la contrabaixista barcelonina Giulia Valle . articles.body: El Sindicat de Llogateres ha instat el govern municipal a aplicar la reserva del 30 % d’habitatge a protecció oficial en noves construccions. Segons ha explicat el seu portaveu, Enric Aragonès , al Bon dia, Barcelona , aquesta mesura podria evitar molts desnonaments, “perquè desincentivaria operacions especulatives tan agressives com comprar un bloc, reformar-lo i fer fora a tothom”. Aragonès també ha carregat contra l’alcalde, Jaume Collboni: “ Va intentar eliminar el decret i, com no se’n va sortir, ara no l’aplica”. Segons el portaveu del sindicat, el problema és que el consistori està centrant els recursos a acompanyar les persones desnonades en el moment de l’expulsió i oferir-los una alternativa residencial, en comptes de centrar-se a aturar els desnonaments . “No es tracta que hi hagi més nits de pensió, sinó que es prenguin mesures amb la mirada llarga “, ha afegit. També et pot interessar Junts vol eliminar el 30 % per a habitatge protegit si és impossible trobar un acord per reformar-lo Roger Torres i Liñán 3 minuts de lectura Més inspeccions dels lloguers de temporada i habitacions Aragonès ha reclamat al govern municipal que faci complir la normativa vigent pel que fa a la regulació dels lloguers de temporada o d’habitacions , ja que és la seva competència. A més, també ha demanat que, més enllà de fer aquestes inspeccions, també informi la ciutadania si hi ha incompliments. “No pot ser que es confiï només en la gent que denuncia un incompliment, perquè un llogater té molta menys força que un arrendador per denunciar-lo “. Per això, reclama campanyes informatives “perquè cap llogater a Barcelona desconegui els seus drets”.
